--- title: "Research" format: html code-fold: true toc: true toc-depth: 2 --- My research focuses on the role of quantitative modelling in public health. I have specific experience working on infectious disease outbreaks, including real-time forecasting and emergency response. My interests are broadly - methods for model evaluation, comparison, and combination (ensemble modelling) - evidence synthesis and expert elicitation, specifically in policy-facing expert advisory groups - evaluating the strengths and weaknesses of modelling as a tool for expert advice ::: {.callout-note title="Experience" collapse="true"} I work in the [Centre for Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Disease](https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/research/centres/centre-mathematical-modelling-infectious-diseases) at the [LSHTM](https://www.lshtm.ac.uk) in London. I've been based in the [epiforecasts](https://epiforecasts.io/) group since 2020. I currently lead a theme of work around outbreak response at LSHTM. I teach across modules in epidemiology and data science, and advocate for an inclusive working environment at my institution, focussing on disability. Previously, I worked on the COVID-19 response, contributing research work to the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies and building modelling infrastructure for the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control. Before training in epidemiology, I worked at the Wellcome Trust across both science funding and the investment portfolio. ::: ::: {.callout-note title="PhD" collapse="true"} I wrote my PhD as work "by publication". This included and evaluated my emergency response work during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2023). My commentary critically reflected the complexities of working in collaborative academic research in response to real-time policy demand. - [Collaborative outbreak modelling for decision support: evaluating trade-offs from multi-model combination](https://researchonline.lshtm.ac.uk/id/eprint/4674767/) ::: ### Recent work ::: {.grid} ::: {.g-col-6} #### Software Software that I've led development or substantially contributed to include: - [Gaza nutrition dashboard](https://cmmid.github.io/gaza-response/) - [Nowcasting and Forecasting of Infectious Disease Dynamics](https://nfidd.github.io/nfidd/) - The [European Modelling Hubs](https://modelling-hubs.ecdc.europa.eu/), specifically - [The European COVID-19 Forecast Hub](https://covid19forecasthub.eu/) - [The European COVID-19 Scenario Hub](https://covid19scenariohub.eu/) - [covidregionaldata](https://epiforecasts.io/covidregionaldata/) All research code is associated with a [Github](https://github.com/kathsherratt) repository, typically under the [epiforecasts](https://github.com/epiforecasts/) organisation. ::: ::: {.g-col-6} #### Papers My publications are available at [Google Scholar](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=sX3wiBAAAAAJ&hl=en), and are open access (please contact me if not available). ::: {.callout-caution title="Selected publications" collapse="true"} ```{.r .cell-code} zotero <- "https://api.zotero.org/" userid <- "users/5456110/" pubs <- "collections/Z3HDMSU9/items/top" params <- "?format=bib&style=feminist-economics&linkwrap=1&locale=en-GB" bib <- readLines(curl::curl(paste0(zotero, userid, pubs, params))) cat(bib) ```
